before.known: but I'm not almost ready to go
before.target: але я не майже готовий іти

after.known: but I'm not ready to go

problem: R8 tier 3: "I'm not almost ready to go" is not natural English, and "не майже" is not a sensible Ukrainian negation of the LEGO.
evidence: The LEGO is "almost ready to go" = "майже готовий іти". Negating "almost" gives a nonsense sentence. The replacement drops the LEGO target, so it fails containment and is probably best deleted.

before.known: I wanted to ask you about something before I had to go
before.target: я хотів запитати тебе про щось перш ніж мені треба йти

after.known: I want to ask you about something before I have to go
after.target: я хочу запитати тебе про щось, перш ніж мені треба йти

problem: Grammar and meaning: the English says "had to go" (past) but the target says "мені треба йти" (present). The tenses disagree.
evidence: The sibling S0025L03 glosses "перш ніж мені треба йти" as "before I have to go" (present).

before.known: she doesn't want to spend too much time reading
before.target: вона не хоче витрачати занадто багато часу, щоб читати

after.known: she doesn't want to spend too much time in order to answer
after.target: вона не хоче витрачати занадто багато часу, щоб відповісти

problem: Meaning: the English says "time reading" but the target says "щоб читати" (in order to read). "Спending time reading" is not the same as "time in order to read".
evidence: S0027L04 teaches "щоб" as "in order to", so "щоб читати" does not match "spend too much time reading".
